paragraphs.text: Cursor limits now depend on which kind of plan you have. Since October 2026, new Cursor subscriptions are part of the X Subscription, a bundle of X Premium, Grok and Cursor sold in five tiers. Older Cursor plans such as Pro, Pro+ and Ultra still work, but they count usage in a different way. This guide explains both, what each plan gets, how to check what you have left and what happens when you hit the limit.

The company now known as SpaceX Super Intelligence announced the X Subscription on October 13, 2026, according to TechCrunch, with a free tier and paid tiers at $8, $30, $100 and $200 a month. Cursor's own documentation lists the same tiers for Cursor.
Cursor limits on the new X Subscription plans

According to Cursor's Models and Pricing page, the plans are Free (limited Agent and Chat use), Plus at $8 a month, Premium at $30 with 4 times the usage of Plus, Super at $100 with 15 times Plus, and Ultra at $200 with 50 times Plus. Paid yearly, they cost $80, $300, $1,000 and $2,000. Teams pay $30, $100 or $200 per seat, matching Premium, Super or Ultra.

Plus is the cheap way in, and it is narrow. It covers only Cursor's own models, with fixed settings: Fast mode off and medium effort. Cursor's docs say Plus does not include Auto, Cloud Agents, Bugbot or your own API keys, and that Plus is not available for teams.

Premium is the first tier that adds Cloud Agents, Automations, Bugbot, Grok Bot and third-party models such as Claude, GPT and Gemini. Those third-party models are not part of the included usage. Cursor bills them at the provider's API list price from prepaid credit, from the first request.
How the weekly pool works

On the X Subscription you get one weekly pool for Cursor models, which the help center lists as Grok 4.7, 4.6, 4.5 and Composer 2.5. The pool resets every week. The same pool is shared with Grok Bot and the Grok apps, so heavy chatting in Grok uses up coding time in Cursor too.

Prepaid credit works differently. It does not reset each week, and each top-up expires 365 days after you buy it, according to Cursor's help center. Credit pays for third-party models and for Cursor models once the weekly pool runs out.

If you code with Claude or GPT models inside Cursor most of the time, compare the price per million tokens first. Cursor lists Composer 2.5 at $0.50 input and $2.50 output per million tokens, and Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 input and $20 output. The same task can cost several times more on a third-party model.
How the legacy Pro, Pro+ and Ultra plans work

Cursor says its older plans (Hobby, Start, Pro, Pro+, Ultra and the Teams Standard and Premium seats) keep working as they are for existing customers. They have two monthly pools: Cursor Models, and Other Models for third-party models at provider prices. Start covers only the Cursor Models pool.

Cursor's legacy pricing page says Pro includes $20 of API agent usage plus bonus usage, Pro+ includes $70 and Ultra includes $400. Legacy pools reset each month, and unused usage does not roll over. Max Mode on older request based plans bills at the API rate plus 20 percent.
How to check your Cursor usage

paragraphs.title: 1. Find out which plan you are on
paragraphs.text: If your plan is called Plus, Premium, Super or Ultra and you pay through X, you are on the X Subscription. If it is called Pro, Pro+, Start or Hobby, you are on a legacy plan.

paragraphs.title: 2. Open the right dashboard
paragraphs.text: For the X Subscription, Cursor's help center points to the Usage section at grok.com/dashboard, and says the editor settings show the same numbers. For legacy plans, open the Spending tab at cursor.com/dashboard/spending.

paragraphs.title: 3. Set a cap before you add credit
paragraphs.text: On the X Subscription you can turn on Auto Top-up, which refills credit when it falls below a threshold you set, and a monthly additional usage limit that caps what you can spend beyond your plan. Both are managed at grok.com/dashboard/billing.
What happens when you hit the limit

Cursor's docs say requests are never downgraded in quality or speed when you run out. On the X Subscription you choose one of three things: wait for the weekly reset, pay from prepaid credit at the same per model rates, or upgrade. On a legacy plan you can turn on on-demand, pay as you go usage or upgrade.

Two smaller rules matter for some people. Your own API keys do not count against included usage on individual plans. Auto in its Cost mode, the classic Auto, is billed as a Cursor model request from your pool, while the other Auto modes are only for Teams and Enterprise.
Which Cursor plan to pick

Plus at $8 fits someone who wants to try agent coding with Cursor's own models and does not need Claude or GPT. Anyone who wants third-party models has to start at Premium and should expect a separate credit bill on top. Super and Ultra make sense only if you hit the Premium pool every week; the dashboard will show that within a week or two.

The weak spot of the new setup is the shared pool. Cursor and the Grok apps draw from the same weekly allowance, so a plan that looks large for coding can run short if you also use Grok a lot. Legacy subscribers keep monthly pools and on-demand billing, so switching is worth doing only after comparing your real monthly usage with the new tiers.
